from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Constant Ratio", ["Circles come in all sizes.", "Diameter and circumference are related.", "The ratio is always constant."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw a large circle in #FFFFFF with radius 2.
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(circle), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight circumference in #FF00FF and diameter in #00FFFF.
        circumference = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(circumference, 'C3')
        diameter = Line(start=circle.get_left(), end=circle.get_right(), color="#00FFFF")
        
        self.play(
            Create(circumference),
            Create(diameter),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show the constant ratio π ≈ 3.14159 in #FFFF00.
        pi_text = MathTex(r"\pi \approx 3.14159", color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(pi_text, 'E3')
        
        self.play(
            Write(pi_text),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00")
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining Pi: The Mathematical Formalization", [
            "Pi is the circle's circumference divided by diameter.",
            "It is an irrational, endless decimal number.",
            "The sequence of digits never repeats."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        circle = Circle(radius=1, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3')
        
        diameter_line = Line(circle.get_left(), circle.get_right(), color=YELLOW)
        c_label = Text("C", color=BLUE).next_to(circle, UP)
        d_label = Text("d", color=YELLOW).next_to(diameter_line, DOWN)
        
        formula = MathTex(r"\pi = \frac{C}{d}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(circle), Create(diameter_line))
        self.play(Write(c_label), Write(d_label))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        pi_val = MathTex(r"\pi \approx 3.14159...", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(pi_val, 'D5')
        self.play(FadeIn(pi_val))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Visual representation of infinity/non-repeating
        dots = Text("...", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(dots, 'E5')
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Archimedes used polygons to estimate Pi.",
            "Polygons inside circles mirror their shape.",
            "More sides mean a closer approximation.",
            "This method was used for centuries.",
            "It eventually led to accurate calculations."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Historical Evolution: The Polygon Method", lecture_lines)
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        square = RegularPolygon(n=4, radius=1.5, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(square, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(circle), Create(square))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Transformation sequence for polygon
        polygon = square
        for n in [8, 16, 32]:
            next_poly = RegularPolygon(n=n, radius=1.5, color=YELLOW)
            self.place_at_grid(next_poly, 'C3')
            self.play(ReplacementTransform(polygon, next_poly))
            polygon = next_poly
            
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        final_poly = RegularPolygon(n=96, radius=1.5, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(final_poly, 'C3')
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(polygon, final_poly))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF69B4"))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Global Perspectives: Ancient Approximations", [
            "Egyptians estimated Pi as 3.16.",
            "Zu Chongzhi calculated Pi very precisely.",
            "Ancient civilizations valued this constant."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        archimedes_val = MathTex(r"\pi \approx \frac{22}{7} \approx 3.1428").set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(archimedes_val, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(archimedes_val))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        zu_val = MathTex(r"\pi \approx \frac{355}{113} \approx 3.1415929").set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(zu_val, 'D4', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(zu_val))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        timeline = Line(start=self.grid['E2'], end=self.grid['E6'], color=WHITE)
        self.play(Create(timeline))
        
        mark1 = Dot(self.grid['E2'], color=BLUE)
        mark2 = Dot(self.grid['E6'], color=GREEN)
        label1 = Text("Egypt", font_size=16).next_to(mark1, DOWN)
        label2 = Text("China", font_size=16).next_to(mark2, DOWN)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(mark1, mark2, label1, label2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Pi is a fundamental universal constant.",
            "Engineers use it for complex designs.",
            "It is essential for space exploration.",
            "Pi connects mathematics to the physical world.",
            "Happy Pi Day to everyone!"
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Application", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define mobjects
        pi_symbol = MathTex(r"\pi", color=YELLOW, font_size=72)
        engineering_icon = Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE, stroke_width=4)
        space_probe = Star(n=5, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).scale(0.5)
        text_universal = Text("Pi is universal", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(pi_symbol, "B3")
        self.play(FadeIn(pi_symbol))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(engineering_icon, "B5")
        self.play(Create(engineering_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.place_at_grid(space_probe, "D3")
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(space_probe))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(text_universal, "E5")
        self.play(FadeIn(text_universal))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(RED))
        celebration = Text("Happy Pi Day!", font_size=32, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(celebration, "F3")
        self.play(Write(celebration))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Mystery of Pi: Definition and History

sections.title: The Hook: The Constant Ratio
sections.content: Introduce the concept that no matter how large or small a circle is, the relationship between its circumference and diameter remains a constant. Use a visual of a rolling tire to establish the prerequisite knowledge: C = πd.
sections.example: An animated unicycle rolling on a path; as the wheel completes one rotation, the distance traveled is exactly π times its diameter.

sections.title: Defining Pi: The Mathematical Formalization
sections.content: Define π (Pi) as the ratio of a circle's circumference (C) to its diameter (d). Explain that since it is an irrational number, its decimal representation never ends or repeats.
sections.example: An interactive graphic showing a circle with diameter '1' being 'unrolled' into a straight line of length '3.14159...'

sections.title: Historical Evolution: The Polygon Method
sections.content: Explain Archimedes' method of 'exhaustion.' Before modern computers, mathematicians approximated π by drawing regular polygons inside and outside a circle. As the number of sides increased, the polygon's perimeter got closer to the circle's circumference.
sections.example: A visual animation showing a square evolving into a hexagon, then a 12-gon, 24-gon, and finally a 96-gon hugging the circle tighter and tighter.

sections.title: Global Perspectives: Ancient Approximations
sections.content: Briefly highlight how different civilizations approached π. Mention the Rhind Papyrus (Egypt) estimating 3.16 and Zu Chongzhi (China) who calculated π to seven decimal places using the 'Liu Hui's Algorithm'.
sections.example: A historical timeline graphic comparing a wooden ancient ruler (Egypt) and a traditional Chinese abacus (Zu Chongzhi) calculating π.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
sections.content: Summarize that π is not just a number, but a fundamental constant of the universe. Preview its applications in engineering, space travel, and quantum physics.
sections.example: A final visual of a space probe calculating its trajectory arc using π, transitioning into a 'Pi Day' celebration icon.
